newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Bank/Portugal to leave rates steady - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Bank/Portugal to leave rates steady - analysts.

text.p: The Bank of Portugal is expected to leave its key rates unchanged tomorrow at the start of a new central bank reserve accounting period, despite the recent strengthening of the escudo against the mark, analysts said.

The central bank was likely to wait for March inflation figures, due in mid-April, before cutting rates, but some analysts did not rule out a surprise cut when it announces new money market conditions at 1415 GMT tomorrow.

Nine out of 10 analysts polled by Reuters said they expected the Bank of Portugal to leave the key repo rate unchanged at 6.50 percent and the draining rate, used to drain funds from the money market, steady at 6.20 percent.
They said they also expected the Bank of Portugal to leave the emergency lending rate steady at 8.30 percent.

One analyst, Martim Amaral Neto of Banco ESSI, said he expected a 25 basis points (bp) cut in the repo rate, a 30 bps cut in the draining rate and a cut of between 30 and 40 bps in the emergency lending rate.

"Considering the extreme caution of the Bank of Portugal and, even though the escudo has been resilient to turbulence in foreign exchange markets, I don't think the central bank will change rates tomorrow," said Ana Paula Carvalho of Banco Portugues de Investimento.
Isabel Cabral of Lisbon broker Fincor said: "The escudo is a little stronger, but the central bank is likely to wait a little longer, at least until the release of March inflation data."
Nuno Godinho, analyst of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said: "Although the escudo has strengthened against the mark recently, I don't see any changes in Portuguese key rates for now.
"But I admit that the Bank of Portugal could give us all a surprise."

Amaral Neto said: "The escudo could easily handle a rate cut, as it has shown greater stability than other southern European currencies recently. The recent appreciation of the escudo will contribute to the increased room for manoeuvre of the central bank."
At 1500 GMT, the escudo stood at 100.42/45 per mark, compared with 100.44/47 at the opening and 100.70/75 on March 18, a day of turbulence on the foreign exchange markets.
Most analysts said that the Bank of Portugal would look closely at the trend in non-tradable goods prices for March.
In February prices rose by 0.2 percent, putting year-on-year inflation at 2.9 percent and average annual inflation at 3.2 percent.
Year-on-year non-tradable goods prices grew by just 4.8 percent in February, compared with 5.1 percent in January after having risen by 0.1 percentage points each month in the previous three months.
"The Bank of Portugal is likely to wait for March inflation, especially non-tradable goods, but I think these will be good numbers," said Isabel Costa of Portuguese bank Finantia.
Portuguese Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco told Reuters in London today that provisional estimates for March inflation were better than expected.
